ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a BJT amplifier circuit can be seen, with the power supply being +16 V. The base is connected by the upper 47 kΩ resistor to +16 V and the lower 7.2 kΩ resistor to ground, forming voltage-divider bias; the input terminal is connected through a coupling capacitor to the base node. The transistor collector is connected through a 10 kΩ resistor to +16 V, and outputs Vout through the coupling capacitor on the right side; the emitter is connected through a 2.2 kΩ resistor to ground. Reasoning: When finding the quiescent DC voltage, the input and output coupling capacitors are open-circuited. According to the voltage-divider bias approximation, ignoring base current, the base voltage is V_B ≈ 16×7.2/(47+7.2) = 2.125 V. The emitter voltage is approximately V_E ≈ V_B − 0.7 = 1.425 V. The emitter current I_E ≈ 1.425/2.2 kΩ = 0.648 mA, and approximately I_C ≈ I_E = 0.648 mA. The voltage drop across the collector 10 kΩ resistor is I_C×10 kΩ ≈ 6.48 V, so the collector voltage V_C ≈ 16 − 6.48 = 9.52 V.

method.method_draft: Convert the image to its DC equivalent by opening the coupling capacitors. Compute the base bias from the 47 kΩ/7.2 kΩ divider: V_B≈16·7.2/(47+7.2). Subtract the diode drop to get V_E≈V_B−0.7. Find emitter current through the 2.2 kΩ resistor and approximate collector current equal to it. Then calculate the collector node voltage using the 10 kΩ collector resistor: V_C≈16−I_C·10 kΩ, giving about 9.52 V.
